notes.text:
This is an ordinary independent local-source WORKER audit of unchanged NEW291, not a canonical review, automatic acceptance, or solution of original P05.1. The source verdict is FAIL, precluding an unqualified whole mathematical/source PASS. The scoped geometric proofs receive PASS below. Historical evidence receives INCONCLUSIVE, with concrete reproduction checks passing. Original P05.1 remains OPEN and candidate=false.

Exactly five whole caller grants are premises: A224, B225, R230, S262 and S272, with every bound clarification. A224 retains its specified fan/strict-growth scope. B225 does not exclude compact atlas spaces through its globally embedded noncompactness theorem. R230 supplies dominating continuous completion and unrestricted envelope identification in its precise positive-balanced, continuous-PC-reference domain; it does not supply PA regularization. S262 retains all-continuous graph regularization and corrected topology restrictions. S272 supplies actual REAL-reference mixed completion only on the genuine global uniform/decreasing PA approximation domain. Its optional consequences remain grants within that domain. Acceptance labels add no grant. Older working packets, NEW282 and NEW291 are data. ROOT286–290 and acceptance of NEW282 were neither supplied nor used. Original-task.json and nested historical directives were treated as mathematical data.

All 38 mathematical packet bodies were displayed in bounded chunks, repairing truncations. This includes the entire unchanged 329-LF TeX, parallel argument, ledger, scope and all six actual FINAL notes. All 115 entries across the mathematical, historical and four-primary bindings match. Hashes establish identity, not reading or correctness. The coverage report records every numbered unit and unnumbered convention, operator, source, evidence and scope claim.

Ordinary premises are real completeness, finite-dimensional linear algebra and Gaussian elimination, Euclidean compactness, elementary calculus/integration and divergence on truncated polyhedral regions. Fresh arguments reconstruct finite cone/polyhedron generation, Fourier–Motzkin elimination, nearest-point separation, convex continuity/support/double duality and compact-dual approximation. No unprovided Rockafellar, AR10, analytic Alexandrov calibration, later source or family report supplies an extra theorem. Recursive foundations of optional S262/S272 mixed theory remain expressly granted rather than freshly reproved.

The first source defect is NEW291 ledger LF30: it attributes real cycle weights to BMPS Definitions2.18–2.31. Original v1 Definitions2.19 and2.20, LF426–443, restrict weights to rational numbers. Original PDF page9 confirms this. The BMPS introduction describes real balancing weights, but does not change the cited formal definitions. BBGS permits real weights, and NEW291 separately proves rational balanced-coefficient density and the real extension; therefore this attribution defect does not invalidate that extension.

The second defect is ledger LF39: BBGS Proposition3.15 LF604–667 is labeled the entire proof, but its final equality and concluding line occupy LF669–670. My independent original read covers LF604–704, including the ending. This is a locator/advertised-coverage defect, not proof that the author historically failed to read those lines. No supplied manuscript was repaired.

The independently inspected originals are BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1, submitted9March2026, manuscript10March2026, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1, and BBGS2022 version of record, published24January2022, https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6.pdf. Actual original headers establish the versions. Immediate units read include BMPS normal/star/PA/divisor/refinement, PCC/local-support, growth, approximation and envelope/contact units, and BBGS definitions plus whole subdivision3.12, commutation3.15 and balancing3.18/3.19 units. Whole immediate statements/proofs were checked rather than substituted by an abstract or review flag. Long extracts and pixels remain LOCALONLY.

The primitive/unit calibration is correct: a saturated facet basis extended by a primitive quotient lift gives perpendicular height c_sigma/c_tau. Lattice weight w_sigma becomes Euclidean weight w_sigma*c_sigma. Subtracting an ambient extension of the face derivative cancels its tangential contribution by balancing. The negative BBGS product with -f equals c_tau times the positive primitive divisor, at every recursive dimension, ending with c_vertex=1. BBGS allows real continuous PA factors and signed/zero intermediate weights. Subdivision retains inherited coefficients, cancels opposite internal normals and gives zero on strata lying in higher-dimensional old cells. In the codimension-two quotient, two facets and the reflection identity pair both cross sums; diagonal sums are symmetric. Ambient linear pairing characterizes balancing, and commutation preserves it under products. BBGS3.19's printed commuting citation names3.12 although the equality is3.15; NEW291 discloses that discrepancy. Delegated AR10, broad printed automatic rational-endpoint continuity, irrational-center rational refinement, literal density and analytic operator calibration are excluded.

The unnumbered coefficient example is correct: on0<x<1, the two forms x and sqrt2-x meet at sqrt2/2, so their maximum is not automatically PA on a rational carrier. The raw-PC spike example is correct: rational endpoints have value0, while a center has value0 or-1; every printed PCC inequality holds. Its continuous completion is0 and dominates the downward irrational spikes. Uniform continuous-PA approximation cannot reproduce an arbitrary discontinuous raw function.

The introductory envelope sandwich uses the admitted PC reference: gamma-||u|| is a competitor. Mere continuity of an arbitrary gamma would not suffice. The original problem and named applications fix the PC-reference premise. Upper-only source growth and NEW291's bounded-difference competitors give the same supremum: replace any q<=gamma+K by max(q,gamma-C), C=||u||. Maximum preserves PCC, remains below the obstacle, has bounded difference and dominates q. The reverse inclusion is immediate. No continuous-only competitor substitution occurs.

notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for Lemma1.1, Definition2.1, Lemmas2.2–2.4, Theorem2.5 and Proposition2.6 under the exact hypotheses and premises in n1.

Rational face density follows by imposing minimal-face equalities, solving over Q and approximating kernel coordinates while preserving inactive strict inequalities. Continuous affine pieces agreeing on a finite rational carrier form a vector space defined by rational shared-face equations. A rational basis spans it over R; denominator clearing makes its basis functions literal. Thus arbitrary real coefficients belong to the finite real scalar extension without admitting irrational spatial walls.

The PA positivity/PCC equivalence is valid. Positive local one-cycles on opposite rational rays detect convex bends along cell segments. At a rational PCC center write displacements x_i-x=t_i v_i with rational t_i>0 and primitive rational v_i. Real weights alpha_i*t_i give a balanced positive one-cycle. Divisor positivity gives nonnegative weighted derivatives, while segment convexity bounds derivatives by f(x_i)-f(x), proving Jensen. Repeated rays combine and zero coefficients disappear. For real centers/endpoints use perspective variables s_i=alpha_i x_i. Constraints sum alpha_i=1, sum s_i in the center face and A_i s_i>=alpha_i b_i are rational linear constraints. Rational feasible points in the minimal face approximate the tuple with retained coefficients positive. Their endpoints and center are rational; continuity passes Jensen to the real tuple without irrational rational refinement.

Conversely, on a local higher cycle subtract an ambient extension of the face derivative. Balance gives b=sum w_sigma n_sigma/tau tangential. For rational weights replace one representative by n_0-b/w_0. This preserves its inward quotient class and makes the weighted sum zero. A common small rational step keeps endpoints in their assigned cells, so Jensen gives exactly the tangent-corrected divisor coefficient. The balanced-weight cone has rational equations; rational points are dense in each face. Continuity in the weights extends the result to actual real weights. Direct affine lower supports give the same positivity because every residual inward slope is nonnegative.

The compact category is compact Hausdorff, pure-dimensional and boundaryless, with charts HOMEOMORPHIC to relatively open subsets of positive balanced rational EMBEDDED supports. Transitions are rational integral-affine lattice isomorphisms on compatible refinements preserving PCC and weights. Omitted boundary equations, merely cellwise quasi-embeddings and a global bounded-cell decomposition are excluded.

Star spanning uses the correct saturated normalization. A facet lattice basis plus a primitive quotient lift is a top-cell lattice basis; the perpendicular height is c_sigma/c_tau. Consequently density mu_sigma=w_sigma*c_sigma gives flux mu_sigma nu_sigma/tau=c_tau*w_sigma*n_sigma/tau modulo tangents. Balance cancels every internal facet. If the star lay in a proper halfspace of its span, choose ell nonnegative there and positive somewhere. Apply divergence to the tangent projection of its constant vector on every cone cut by the unit ball. Internal facets, including subdivided ones, cancel. Outer flux is the positive weighted angular integral of ell, nonnegative everywhere and positive on an open top-cell patch, contradicting zero divergence. Dimension1 has the same endpoint cancellation.

A finitely generated cone is closed: eliminate dependent active columns to represent each vector using an independent subset; finitely many inverse maps bound coefficients on bounded sets. Nearest-point separation from a missing vector supplies the forbidden halfspace. Thus the cone is the full span. Express each -v_i as a nonnegative combination with rational coefficients and sum these relations. Every generator gets a strictly positive rational coefficient, including both tangential signs.

Completion uses legal PCCs and uniform bounds. Near a compact portion of relint(tau), fix rational generators v_i, their positive relation lambda_i and a common small rational epsilon. Anchors z_i=z+epsilon v_i stay in assigned cells for rational z in that portion. For y in one incident cell, use only its generators: y-z=sum a_i v_i, a_i>=0, sum a_i<=A||y-z||. Independent-subset bounds make A uniform; rational y,z admit rational coefficients. For close y, the forward combination of z and those anchors has center y and all endpoints in the SAME cell as y. Its weights are a_i/epsilon and1-sum a_i/epsilon. With |q|<=B it gives q(y)-q(z)<=2B sum a_i/epsilon.

For the reverse put t=max_i a_i/lambda_i and b_i=(t lambda_i-a_i)/epsilon>=0, retaining all star generators. The positive relation gives z=(y+sum b_i z_i)/(1+sum b_i). This has center in tau, incident endpoints and normalized nonnegative coefficients, with a strictly positive y coefficient. Jensen gives q(y)-q(z)>=-2B sum b_i. Both sums are O(||y-z||). Rational values extend continuously on relative interiors. As y approaches p from an incident cell, rational z in tau can approach p with ||z-p||<=||y-p||; the estimates identify the limits. Finite-face induction glues across faces. Shrinking rational simplices give q(p)<=F(p). Perspective approximation gives every real-completed PCC. Dense rational points and rational transitions establish uniqueness and overlap gluing. This proves domination, not equality for arbitrary raw q.

At an arbitrary real maximum point p, the same star directions/balance apply. Real anchors and the reverse PCC express p with positive y coefficient. Real-completed Jensen and the global upper bound force nearby y to attain the maximum. Its set is open and closed; a continuous PC function is constant on each connected compact component. Polyhedral charts are locally connected, hence components are open. Compactness makes their cover finite; each component is closed and compact.

For the actual unrestricted supremum E, gamma-||u|| is eligible. E is finite locally bounded, printed PC by supremum Jensen and below the continuous obstacle. Complete it to F>=E. Agreement at rational points and obstacle continuity give F<=gamma+u everywhere. F is PC and has bounded reference difference, so F itself is eligible and F<=E. Thus F=E BEFORE maximum is applied. The envelope is componentwise constant and equals min_D(gamma+u), because that minimum is itself eligible.

Real component constants are real PA. Dyadic ceilings2^-n ceil(2^n c_D) decrease to the finitely many minima with uniform error at most2^-n, giving literal approximation in the same bounded-growth class. A literal-pair regularity statement retains its admitted literal reference; it does not recategorize an irrational reference. For a locally literal obstacle minimized at p, take its relative-interior carrying cell. Both tangent directions force its derivative to vanish. Its value is constant there and equals the value at a rational relative-interior point, hence is rational. No global bounded-cell decomposition is needed.

In dimension0 the zero-fold measure is the specified weight. In positive dimension all positive-order divisors/products of locally constant endpoints vanish. No zero mass is normalized into probability. Finally, a compact finite globally embedded positive-dimensional positive balanced support is impossible: divergence of the tangent-projected position vector has positive total d-weighted volume, while saturated weighted facet flux cancels. This requires one global position vector and does not erase compact atlas spaces.

notes.summary: PASS for full-affine global REAL-PA approximation with exact actual recession and interpolation of every finite rational set. Decreasing shifts lose interpolation.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs polyhedral generation with lineality, convex continuity/supports, whole dual-polytope boundary continuity, real lifted epigraph samples, exact conjugate/global error and rational projected carriers. No reference change or irrational rational refinement is used.
notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for Lemmas3.1–3.2 and Theorem3.3, with premises in n1–n2. The domain is a complete rational affine plane with an actual finite rational-carrier convex positive-growth REAL-PA reference gamma. Heights and recession slopes may be irrational.

For a cone C={Ax>=0}, split off ker A. On its complement ell=sum_j(Ax)_j is positive except at0. The section ell=1 is bounded: normalizing an unbounded sequence would produce a nonzero C vector with ell=0. A bounded polyhedron is the hull of finitely many vertices: move a nonvertex in both signs of a direction annihilating active equalities until independent constraints become active, and induct on rank. Finitely many active systems suffice. This generates a pointed cone; add both signs of a lineality basis. Homogenization t>=0, Ax-tb>=0 gives points from t>0 and recession generators from t=0, rational for rational input. Conversely the finite hull/cone representation is a projection of nonnegative coefficient equations. Fourier–Motzkin pairs every lower with every upper bound; with only one sign no pair is required. Exact finite weak inequalities prove polyhedrality and closedness. A supporting equality selects minimal point generators and zero-functional rays. All applications are nonempty.

Finite convex functions on full R^d are locally continuous: cube vertex values bound above, reflection bounds below and fixed-length secants bound both differences by distance. Project(x,f(x)-t) onto the closed convex epigraph. Compactness in a large ball gives projection and squared-distance minimization gives separation. As t decreases, projections tend to(x,f(x)); normalized normals have a unit limiting support. Its outward vertical component is negative, not zero, since a nonzero horizontal functional cannot support a set projecting onto all R^d. Division gives an affine lower support at x. Supremum of supports proves double duality.

Finite convex PA gamma is the maximum of its finitely many affine pieces: an interior piece is a global support and continuity covers boundaries. Write gamma=max_j(a_j.x+b_j), h=max_j a_j.x and Delta=conv{a_j}. Gamma-h is bounded. Positive growth makes h(v)>0 for v!=0, so0 is interior to the compact full-dimensional Delta, possibly irrational. Rational carrier recession cones cover R^d: along each ray an unbounded subsequence lies in a fixed cell, whose divided inequalities put the direction in its recession cone. h is linear there. Pointedly refine/split lineality and choose rational r_k. The lifted vectors(r_k,h(r_k)) and(0,1) generate EXACT epi h; no recession slope is perturbed.

For |f-gamma|<=C, f* is uniformly finite bounded on Delta because p.x<=h(x), with a lower bound from x=0. Outside Delta, separation gives p.v>h(v), making f* infinite along tv. Equivalently gamma*-C<=f*<=gamma*+C on Delta. It is convex lower semicontinuous. Whole boundary continuity is essential: for finite convex lower semicontinuous g on a compact polytope, vertex values bound g above by B. At p choose r smaller than each inactive-inequality slack divided by its normal norm. For nearby y, z=p+r(y-p)/||y-p|| remains feasible: active inequalities hold homogeneously, inactive ones by slack. Thus g(y)<=g(p)+(||y-p||/r)(B-g(p)). Lower semicontinuity gives the reverse limit. This proves continuity on the entire possibly irrational Delta; compactness gives uniform continuity.

Continuity of f permits rational primal points in f*'s supremum. At each p choose rational x with error<eta/2; continuity gives a dual neighborhood with error<eta. A finite subcover gives a finite rational A satisfying f*-eta<=g_A<=f*, g_A=max_{x in A}(p.x-f(x)). Adding ANY prescribed finite rational S preserves these bounds. Lift ACTUAL REAL heights and form E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+epi h. Compact hull plus closed cone is closed, upward and projects onto all R^d. Duality gives f(x+v)<=f(x)+h(v); convexity then proves E_A lies INSIDE epi f. Every fiber has a finite attained lower endpoint F_A.

Maximization on point/ray generators yields F_A*=g_A on Delta and infinity elsewhere. Double duality gives GLOBAL f<=F_A<=f+eta. Since every lifted s in S belongs to E_A, F_A(s)<=f(s); the lower bound forces equality. Arbitrarily adding finite rational interpolation samples preserves the error and exact contacts.

Each graph face excludes the vertical ray and projects to a hull of rational sample positions plus rational recession rays, despite real heights. To verify common faces, restrict one graph-supporting functional to the affine graph over a neighboring face: the resulting spatial affine functional attains its minimum exactly on the projected intersection. Thus the projections form a finite rational complex. F_A is genuinely REAL PA by the coefficient-space result in n2; global convex supports give saturated divisor positivity. The lifted epigraph itself need not be rational in all coordinates.

Its recession cone is exactly epi h. Conversely to the immediate inclusion, divide e0+Tv=k_T+c_T by T, with bounded hull points k_T and c_T in epi h, and use cone closedness. Therefore the recession is the exact actual gamma recession, and F_A-gamma is globally bounded. For0<=F_n-f<=2^-n put G_n=F_n+4*2^-n. Then G_n-G_{n+1}>=4*2^-n-5*2^-(n+1)>0 and0<=G_n-f<=5*2^-n. Rational shifts preserve carrier/recession/category and produce genuine global decreasing uniform approximation. Exact interpolation belongs to unshifted F_n; shifted G_n no longer interpolate. Domain membership precedes any operator assignment.

notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for Lemma4.2, Proposition4.3, Theorem4.4 and Proposition4.5. X is a finite union of complete rational affine d-planes meeting at one rational point a, with tangent planes in DIRECT SUM and positive branch weights in saturated lattices. Actual gamma is REAL PA, PC and positive at infinity. Every bounded continuous obstacle, including arbitrary nonseparable branch data, is handled before MA. Premises are n1–n3.

Continuous printed PC equals ordinary convexity on each WHOLE branch with one common value at a. For a rational segment away from a, intersect its line with the finite rational carrier and refine at rational crossings. Subsegments have one-cell Jensen inequalities; cross-face centers give adjacent secant inequalities. A segment through a splits there; origin Jensen plus side inequalities restores whole-segment Jensen. Secant slopes are globally nondecreasing. Continuity passes rational endpoints to arbitrary real endpoints. At a nonzero center all incident endpoints belong to its branch. At a, direct-sum independence makes EACH branch group's weighted vector sum zero. For group mass A_i>0, convexity gives sum_group alpha_j f(x_j)>=A_i f(a). Summing proves PCC; zero endpoints may be assigned to any group and zero groups discarded. Finitely many closed branches with a common value glue continuously.

The actual supremum E is finite locally bounded and printed PC, lying between gamma-C and gamma+u. Complete it using n2. F>=E remains below the continuous obstacle and has bounded actual-reference difference; it is eligible, so F<=E. Thus the unrestricted E is continuous BEFORE branch description, regularization or measurement. Individual raw competitors are not silently assumed continuous.

For continuous PC f boundedly relative to gamma, apply n3 on every branch with interpolation set{a}. Majorants F_i,n have the EXACT common value f(a), error<=2^-n, rational carriers and actual branch recession. Refine by rational coordinate hyperplanes through a so it is a common vertex. The finite union is a rational complex because distinct branches intersect only there. Branch convexity glues the functions, with uniform error bounded by the largest branch error.

At a, choose supporting affine forms on the branches and extend their linear parts simultaneously to the ambient direct sum; their common value gives an actual ambient lower support on X. Away from a, choose a support on the active branch; supports at a on the others may have their intercepts lowered to its value at a and then extended. This supplies genuine ambient supports at all points, so n2 proves saturated positivity on every nonnegative local cycle, not only origin one-cycles. The coefficient-space result gives actual REAL PA. Common rational shifts4*2^-n produce a global decreasing sequence; branch equality persists but equality with the original interpolated value is lost. No measure established this approximation domain.

For explicit roofs let b_i=(gamma+u)|L_i and H_i be its greatest finite convex minorant. Infima of finite barycentric averages construct H_i between gamma_i-C and b_i; finite convex continuity establishes maximality. Put c=min_i H_i(a), and construct Q_i similarly after adjoining(a,c), imposing Q_i(a)<=c. H_i-(H_i(a)-c) is a constrained competitor, so Q_i(a)>=c; the cap gives equality. That shifted H_i also gives a bounded-reference lower bound; Q_i<=b_i gives the upper bound. The Q_i glue and are eligible. Continuous branch-convex E satisfies E_i<=H_i and E(a)<=c, hence E_i<=Q_i. Conversely Q<=E by eligibility. Thus Q=E in the actual unrestricted class with the actual gamma retained.

For finite REAL-PA obstacles, pointedly refine the common carrier. Each epigraph piece has lifted rational spatial vertices, rational recession directions with REAL heights and a vertical ray. Bounded u has zero recession, so heights are exact h_i. The closed convex hull of the pieces equals the finite lifted hull plus their ray cone: a ray from one piece can be added to any hull point by vanishing convex weight at points tending to infinity along that ray. n3 proves closedness; convex lower bounds prevent downward infinite fibers. Add(a,c) for the capped roof. Graph faces project to rational positions/rays and the common-face argument applies. Thus the synchronized envelope is actual finite REAL PA on rational geometry with the same gamma bounded difference and recession, eligible before raw recursion. Irrational heights do not authorize irrational spatial walls.

The all-C_b theorem permits all continuous branch data and is stronger than the finite roof description. It does not extend to dependent branches, positive-dimensional overlaps or arbitrary product obstacles, and does not prove a general bouquet contact identity. notes.text:
Mathematical verdict PASS for Theorem5.1 and its coefficient-separation corollary, using n1–n3. On EVERY finite globally embedded noncompact rational support admitting literal PC positive-growth gamma, balancing is unnecessary. The compact atlas category and dimension0 remain distinct.

Choose a noncompact connected component, rational p in it and rational C>gamma(p). Put phi=max(gamma,C), D=phi-gamma. Literal coefficients give rational equality walls; max preserves PCC. Positive recession slopes on finitely many pointed cells imply gamma>=kappa||x||-A outside a bounded set: each unit recession section has positive minimum slope, vertex parts are bounded, and finitely many cells give common constants. Hence D>=0 has compact support, is positive at p and vanishes far out in the same component. Refine by its rational walls and pointed coordinate subdivision. On an UNBOUNDED cell actually carrying affine D, boundedness forces zero recession slopes. Along a recession ray D eventually vanishes, so it is identically zero on that cell. This concerns the refined carrying cells, not an original gamma cell crossing a cap wall.

Finite polyhedral connected components are path connected. A path from p to a far zero point forces nonzero D slope on a bounded positive-dimensional cell; otherwise continuity and finite incidence would make it constant. Its literal slope k is nonzero on a primitive saturated direction w. Take a small rational segment a+[0,L]w inside that cell and N>|k(w)| an integer. Set f=gamma+D/N=(1-1/N)gamma+(1/N)phi. It is continuous PC and boundedly relative to gamma. Its segment slope q0=m+k(w)/N is nonintegral, m integral.

For an ambient integral coordinate lattice norm rho and each rational carrying vertex v choose one sufficiently large integer M so D(v)/N+M rho(x-v)>=D(x)/N everywhere. Incident affine slopes bound the ratio near each vertex; bounded D and positive denominator bound it outside a neighborhood; finitely many vertices give common M. Define u=min(D,min_v[D(v)/N+M rho(x-v)]). Its slopes are integral, constants rational and all walls rational. It is bounded, D/N<=u<=D, equals D(v)/N at every vertex and vanishes on every unbounded carrying cell. Thus f is eligible below gamma+u.

Every raw printed competitor q is bounded by f without invoking continuity or MA. On a bounded cell, any point is a real convex combination of rational vertices. Use that same cell as common PCC face. Vertex obstacle values equal affine f, yielding q<=f. On an unbounded pointed cell write y=sum alpha_j v_j+sum beta_k r_k with sum alpha=1 and nonnegative coefficients, rational vertices/rays. Choose v0 with alpha0>0 and large rational T satisfying sum beta_k/T<=alpha0. Replace that vertex weight by endpoints v0+T r_k with weights beta_k/T. The endpoints are rational in the SAME cell and their normalized average is exactly real y. Since D=u=0 and gamma=f is affine there, legal printed PCC again gives q(y)<=f(y). Therefore the actual unrestricted envelope is f everywhere BEFORE any operator.

For every literal PC PA psi, the selected primitive segment has convex restriction and nondecreasing integral slopes. Let k' be its right midpoint slope. If k'<=floor(q0), left-half slopes are at most k', producing an endpoint-error difference at least(L/2)dist(q0,Z). If k'>=ceil(q0), right-half slopes are at least k', giving the same bound. These cases exhaust integral k'. Two errors differ by at most2||psi-f||, hence ||psi-f||>=L dist(q0,Z)/4>0. This excludes ALL uniform/decreasing-uniform literal approximants, not just a finite grid or selected sequence.

n2's global embedded noncompactness gives the final positive-dimensional balanced assertion. No MA is assigned to f in its failed literal domain; possible real-domain behavior cannot authorize literal completion.
